source.title: Mechanically induced localisation of SECONDARY WALL INTERACTING bZIP is associated with thigmomorphogenic and secondary cell wall gene expression

value: 8,902, 5,682 and 7,672 root transcripts differentially expressed at 10, 30 and 60 min after touch
method: RNA-seq of Bd21-3 roots sampled before touch and at 10, 30 and 60 min after touch applied with a metal probe along the whole root
conditions: Accession Bd21-3, wildtype; seedlings 6 days old on vertical 1X MS agar; touch with a metal probe along the entire root, force and stroke number for this transcriptome not stated (the localisation assay used a blunt probe five times in about 5 s); 3 roots pooled per biological replicate, 3 biological replicates per sample; counts pool up- and down-regulated transcripts (the text does not split them); the same paragraph reports that SWIZ-OE roots already differed by 11,488 genes from untouched wildtype before touch; PC1 (60%) separated genotypes and PC2 (17%) separated pre-touch from 10 min after touch.
where: Section 2.3, Results (text sentence with Supplemental Tables S2 to S4); sampling in Methods
quote: The wildtype transcriptome underwent significant remodelling in response to touch, with 8,902 transcripts differentially expressed (q < 0.1) at 10 min post-touch, 5,682 transcripts at 30 min and 7,672 transcripts at 60 min (Supplemental Tables S2–S4).
note: WFO: wfoplantlist.org/taxon/wfo-0000854379-2025-06 (opened) Brachypodium distachyon (L.) Touch-induced gene expression in a grass; counts only, no direction in the quoted sentence.

source.title: Mechanically induced localisation of SECONDARY WALL INTERACTING bZIP is associated with thigmomorphogenic and secondary cell wall gene expression

value: SWIZ (a bZIP transcription factor) moved from cytoplasm to nucleus in root cells after each mechanical stimulation
method: confocal imaging of SWIZ:GFP-OE roots with a blunt-probe stimulus applied in the field of view at 0, 90 and 180 min
conditions: Transgenic SWIZ:GFP overexpression line in Bd21-3, so localisation of the fusion protein under overexpression, not native protein; stimulus at 0, 90 and 180 min, n = 126 nuclei (Figure 1d legend); Figure 1b legend n = 14 to 20 nuclei and n = 4 to 6 plants per treatment, no statistical test named in the legend; the text for Figure 1b adds that the nuclear GFP signal peaked about 30 min after a stimulus, returned to near basal levels by about 60 min, and that untouched plants showed no change in localisation; the paper reports translocation only in the touched root region; stimulus was about five probe strokes in about 5 s, force not measured.
quote: Following each mechanical stimulation, SWIZ consistently translocated from cytoplasm to the nucleus (Figure 1d).
note: WFO: wfoplantlist.org/taxon/wfo-0000854379-2025-06 (opened) Brachypodium distachyon (L.) P.Beauv. accepted, id wfo-0000854379, June 2025 snapshot; POWO: powo.science.kew.org/taxon/393098-1 (opened) 'This species is accepted'. source.title: Mechanically induced localisation of SECONDARY WALL INTERACTING bZIP is associated with thigmomorphogenic and secondary cell wall gene expression

value: wildtype stems shorter after 2 weeks of metal-bar touch than controls, and shorter still after 3 weeks
units: qualitative (heights in Supplemental Figure S8A-B, not stated in text)
method: Thigmomatic robot sweeping plants with a metal bar once every 90 min for 2 or 3 weeks; stem height compared with untouched controls
conditions: Bd21-3 wildtype per Results (Methods give no genotype for this experiment); plant age at start, n and statistical test not stated in the text; bar swept a set distance in one direction every 90 min. Contrary or null results in the same section: despite the height difference there was no significant difference in aboveground biomass (S8C); 3-week plants had significantly more branches (S8D); third elongated internode and peduncle cross sections showed no significant difference in cell wall thickness or phloroglucinol staining in response to touch (S8E-G).
quote: Two-week stressed plants were significantly shorter than control plants, and 3-week stressed plants were shorter still (Supplemental Figure S8A-B).
